title: Homotopy-commuting invariance of path-model pullbacks
statement:
Use simplicial sets, spaces, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Work in its fixed containing universe. Let $u:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, $u':U'\to W'$, and $v':V'\to W'$ be maps of Kan complexes. Let $a:U\to U'$, $b:V\to V'$, and $c:W\to W'$ be weak homotopy equivalences. Suppose specified simplicial homotopies are given from $c\circ u$ to $u'\circ a$ and from $c\circ v$ to $v'\circ b$. Write
$$P(u,v)=U\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_1}V,$$
with paths directed from $u(x)$ to $v(y)$, and define $P(u',v')$ similarly. There exists a simplicial comparison sending $(x,y,\gamma)$ to $(a(x),b(y),H_u(x)^{-1}*c(\gamma)*H_v(y))$, where $H_u,H_v$ are the specified homotopies and $*$ is coherent path concatenation, which is a weak homotopy equivalence. Coherent concatenation means choosing composition triangles in the Kan complex, simultaneously on the whole parameter simplicial set; any such coherent choice gives the same comparison up to homotopy. The construction retains all parameter simplices and further homotopies of the displayed data.

source.place: Agent-formulated homotopy-commuting extension of Kerodon Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B), using the path model of Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B), the fiber criterion of Proposition 3.3.7.1 (00ZN), and coherent composition of Subsection 4.6.8 (01PF). Proposition 032B itself assumes strict commutation; the specified endpoint homotopies and simultaneous coherent choices are the additional assertion of this node. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: First apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the strictly commuting map of spans with vertical maps $1_U,c,1_V$. It gives a weak equivalence $q:P(u,v)\to Q_0=P(cu,cv)$ sending $\gamma$ to $c\gamma$. Put $X=U\times V$, $I=\Delta^1$, $B=W'\times W'$, and $l_0=(cu,cv):X\to B$, $l_1=(u'a,v'b):X\to B$. The given homotopies define the simplicial map $G:X\times I\to B$, $G(x,y,t)=(H_u(x,t),H_v(y,t))$. Its endpoint restrictions are exactly $l_0,l_1$. It remains to construct an endpoint-adjustment weak equivalence $Q_0\to Q_1=P(u'a,v'b)$ and then apply the same strict-span invariance with vertical maps $a,1_{W'},b$ to $Q_1\to P(u',v')$. Both uses have Kan vertices and weak-equivalence vertical maps as required.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9, strict-span comparisons before and after the endpoint-adjustment construction (agent expansion).

proof.text: Let $e:\operatorname{Fun}(I,W')\to B$ restrict to the two endpoints. A horn lifting problem for $e$ transposes to extension into $W'$ from $(\partial I\times\Delta^n)\cup(I\times\Lambda_k^n)$ inside $I\times\Delta^n$. This is the pushout-product of the monomorphism $\partial I\hookrightarrow I$ and a horn inclusion. The latter is anodyne by the defining lifting property of Kan fibrations; the cited pushout-product result therefore supplies the extension because $W'$ is Kan. Thus $e$ is a Kan fibration. Set $E=(X\times I)\times_{B,G,e}\operatorname{Fun}(I,W')$ and let $p:E\to X\times I$ be projection. Any horn square for $p$ projects to one for $e$ and its filler pairs with the already prescribed base simplex, so $p$ is a Kan fibration. Its pullback along $j_i:X\to X\times I$, $j_i(z)=(z,i)$, is precisely $Q_i$ for $i=0,1$. Denote the inclusions by $J_i:Q_i\to E$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.3, endpoint case; explicit product/exponential adjunction and pullback lifting calculation.

proof.text: Each $j_i$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Indeed its retraction is the projection to $X$. The monotone maps $\min,\max:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ induce simplicial homotopies between the identity of $X\times I$ and the appropriate constant-endpoint retraction composite. For every Kan target $Z$, a homotopy $L$ of maps induces a homotopy of precomposition maps by $(\psi,t)\mapsto\psi L_t$, hence equal functions on edge components. Projection and $j_i$ therefore induce inverse bijections on these component sets, and [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] applies. Now apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance] to the cospans $E\xrightarrow{p}X\times I\xleftarrow{j_i}X$ and $E\xrightarrow{p}X\times I\xleftarrow{1}X\times I$, with vertical maps $1_E,1_{X\times I},j_i$. Their left legs are the Kan fibration $p$ in both rows. Their pullbacks are $Q_i$ and $E$, and the induced map is $J_i$. Consequently both $J_0$ and $J_1$ are weak equivalences. No Kan condition on $X\times I$ or $E$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.2 applied to endpoint inclusions; explicit simplicial contractions and Kan-target testing show its weak-equivalence hypotheses.

proof.text: Write $r:Q_0\to X$ for projection. Since $\{0\}\hookrightarrow I$ is a horn inclusion, its pushout-product with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Q_0$ is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Lift against $p$ with upper map $J_0:Q_0\times\{0\}\to E$ and lower map $(z,t)\mapsto(r(z),t)$ into $X\times I$. This gives $L:Q_0\times I\to E$ with $L|_0=J_0$. At $t=1$ it factors, degree by degree, uniquely as $J_1\tau$ for a simplicial map $\tau:Q_0\to Q_1$ over $X$. Thus $L$ is the required specified homotopy $J_0\simeq J_1\tau$. Its path coordinate is a map $Q_0\times I_t\times I_s\to W'$ whose edges at $s=0,1$ are $H_u,H_v$ and whose edges at $t=0,1$ are the universal input path and the output path. The construction is on the entire simplicial set $Q_0$, not on its vertices.

source.place: Agent endpoint-homotopy lifting argument from the same pushout-product lifting calculation as Corollary 3.1.3.3.

proof.text: For each Kan target $Z$, the homotopy $L$ in step 4 identifies the precomposition functions of $J_0$ and $J_1\tau$ on edge-component sets: postcompose $L$ with a simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(E,Z)$ and use the internal functor adjunction. Since $J_0$ is a weak equivalence, its testing function is bijective, so $J_1\tau$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence]. The testing function of $J_1$ is also bijective by step 3. The equation $(J_1\tau)^*=\tau^*J_1^*$ then implies that $\tau^*$ is bijective for every Kan $Z$, so $\tau$ is a weak equivalence. Finally the strictly commuting span map with vertical maps $a,1_{W'},b$ gives a weak equivalence $s:Q_1\to P(u',v')$ by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]. The desired map is $s\tau q$, which is a weak equivalence because its testing functions are composites of bijections.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9 for the last strict comparison; the intervening cancellation is written using Kan-target testing.

proof.text: Here is the path formula and its coherent meaning. Write $\eta$ for the universal path on $Q_0$; after precomposition with $q$ it is $c\gamma$. In the square of step 4 put $A=cu(x)$, $B_0=cv(y)$, $A'=u'a(x)$, $B'=v'b(y)$. The triangle with vertices $A,B_0,B'$ has edges $\eta,H_v$ and a diagonal $d$. The triangle with vertices $A,A',B'$ has edges $H_u,\tau(\gamma)$ and that same diagonal. Thus these two triangles witness $H_u*\tau(\eta)=\eta*H_v$, which is the formula $\tau(\eta)=H_u^{-1}*\eta*H_v$ in coherent path notation. There is no reversal map of the directed simplex being used. Conversely, these two triangles can be chosen directly, first by filling $Q_0\times\Lambda_1^2\hookrightarrow Q_0\times\Delta^2$, then by filling $Q_0\times\Lambda_0^2\hookrightarrow Q_0\times\Delta^2$. Both inclusions are anodyne by the pushout-product result with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Q_0$, and the second horn has its two edges with common source $A$. Gluing the triangles gives exactly a square lift as in step 4. This realizes the formula simultaneously on all parameter simplices.

source.place: Subsection 4.6.8 motivates coherent composition; here the two explicit parameterized horn fillings prove the required path formula directly.

proof.text: To check independence and higher compatibility, let $K\hookrightarrow M$ be any monomorphism of parameter simplicial sets, and suppose square lifts of the fixed data are already prescribed over $K$. Extending them over $M$ is a lifting problem against $p$ with domain $(Q_0\times I\times K)\cup(Q_0\times\{0\}\times M)$ inside $Q_0\times I\times M$; its base map is $(z,t,m)\mapsto(r(z),t)$. The domain inclusion is, after permuting factors, the pushout-product of $Q_0\times K\hookrightarrow Q_0\times M$ with $\{0\}\hookrightarrow I$. It is anodyne by the cited result, so a lift exists. With $K=\partial\Delta^1$ and $M=\Delta^1$, any two square choices are joined, and their endpoint restrictions give a homotopy $\tau_0\simeq\tau_1$ over $X$. With $K=\partial\Delta^n$, all prescribed compatible higher comparison homotopies extend as well. For data varying over a parameter simplicial set $M$, let $Q_M$ be the total simplicial set of initial paths with their parameter, and let $Q_K\hookrightarrow Q_M$ be its restriction to a parameter subcomplex $K$. The initial and previously chosen lifts define a map on $(Q_M\times\{0\})\cup(Q_K\times I)$; its inclusion into $Q_M\times I$ is the pushout-product of $Q_K\hookrightarrow Q_M$ with $\{0\}\hookrightarrow I$. Lift against the endpoint fibration $e$ using the actual varying endpoint homotopies as base map. This proves the relative family assertion without identifying different fibers of $Q_M$. The two horn-filling stages of step 6 have the same relative extension property, using their horn inclusions in place of $\{0\}\hookrightarrow I$. Hence alternative coherent triangle choices and further homotopies are retained, not just equality of pointwise homotopy classes.

source.place: Agent relative-parameter pushout-product argument, including uniqueness up to homotopy and all higher prescribed boundary compatibilities.

proof_origin.place: Agent proof extending the strict comparison of 032B: lift the endpoint homotopy through the endpoint path fibration, use 0109 on its endpoint pullbacks, and prove relative choice coherence by pushout-products. Kerodon read online; archival copy WANTED in report.

The two-triangle square gives tau(eta) = H_u^{-1}*eta*H_v with the correct direction u'a(x)->v'b(y).
